title: Lodging problems for black bands before integration
summary: Before the civil rights act, black bands struggled to find hotels; schoolhouse cafeterias fed them.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah, well, was that a recurring problem, when you sent bands on the road, black bands on the road?
At that particular time as well. It was bad.
Would you always have problems with where they were going to stay?

We did, before they passed the bill, yes. We did, before they passed the bill. Because, see, you'd have to find, either the bus station, you'd have to find some of those small rustling, and a lot of these small towns that ain't had no rustling, you know. They didn't have them. So it was a problem, it was a problem.
I mean, any band knowing that they would go on the road?
Right. Now a lot of the schoolhouses, we would eat in the cafeteria at the schoolhouses, you see.
